evidence.title: 02 · Analyse data, graphs and uncertainty
teachingSections: Choose a graph for the variables
Discrete and continuous variables determine representation
Construct a frequency table using stated boundaries
Calculate quartiles with an explicit convention
Build and interpret a line of best fit
Translate between a graph, equation and biological statement
Probability and numerical uncertainty need context
practiceQuestions: A quantity rises from 40 to 50. Calculate percentage increase.
How would you improve a method with a consistently miscalibrated sensor?
A sensor displays 0.01 g increments. Why is a reported change of 0.0003 g unsupported by that display alone?
For ordered values 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 18, calculate IQR using median-of-halves.
A best-fit line for a teaching dataset passes through (2 min, 90 beats min⁻¹) and (6 min, 66 beats min⁻¹). Calculate the gradient.
What makes a histogram boundary convention useful?
State a specific improvement for random timing variation and one for systematic calibration error.
Convert 18% to a simplified fraction, then express 9 affected and 36 unaffected as a ratio and affected percentage.
Construct a histogram from frequencies 4, 4 and 2 for intervals 50–<60, 60–<70 and 70–<80. Explain why the bars touch.
Construct a scatter plot for recovery time 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 min and pulse 105, 98, 89, 82, 76, 71, 68 beats min⁻¹. Add an appropriate fitted trend and interpret it.
A category frequency table has counts 4, 4 and 2 from ten observations. Calculate pie-chart angles.
Explain accuracy, precision and resolution using a balance that repeats 5.20 g for a certified 5.00 g mass.
